title: Handlebar Remote
tagline: A slim thumb controller between the grip and the switch cube, for the dash and your phone
summary: One slim collar on the left handlebar, between the grip and the bike's switch cube: a 5-way joystick at the back under your thumb and 4 buttons going up over the top of the bar, on a face curved round the bar and tilted toward the grip, so nothing stands higher than the switch cube and it hides none of the bike's own instruments. The electronics sit in a slim bay underneath. It works the Handlebar Dash over its own wiring (one of the dash's expansion slots) and a phone or anything else over Bluetooth, as a keyboard with media keys. One smooth, rounded body: the switches in 2 printed carriers inside the face, a printed TPU keypad that seals it, the halves hinged at the back and closed by one hidden screw. General purpose: the bar size, the gap and the angles are settings.
status: Designed and modelled (v1, checked in CAD, not printed or built yet). The switches and boards have no published drawings: measure yours first, and the gap you can make between the grip and the switch cube. The firmware comes next.
see_sub: One smooth collar, 19 mm wide, in a 20 mm gap between the grip and the switch cube (slide the cube inboard to make it): the controls on a face curved round the back and the top of the bar, its highest point 27.7 mm above the bar's centre (the cube's top is at 30); the ESP32-C3 and the CAN transceiver in the bay underneath.

gallery.caption: From the rider's seat: the collar between the grip and the switch cube (grey: a stand-in; measure yours), no higher than the cube: the joystick at the back under the thumb, the buttons over the top, the bay underneath
From the rider's side: the joystick at the back, buttons 1 and 2 (round) and 3 and 4 (pills) going up over the bar, each in its own cup, a ridge between 2 and 3
Along the bar: the face curves round the back and the top of the bar, the joystick at the back; the hinge below it, the bay turned a little forward
From above: 19 mm wide along the bar, in the gap between the grip and the switch cube
The bay under the bar, opened: the ESP32-C3 and the CAN transceiver on edge side by side, its cap and gasket below
Taken apart: the collar's top half (with the face) lifted, the keypad, the 2 switch carriers with their switches, the joystick's cap, the bottom half swung open on its hinge, the bay's gasket and cap

docs.label: README: what it does, how it's built, the wiring and the dash-bus messages

collar_top.name: Collar top (with the face)
collar_top.what: The smooth body's upper half: the ring's top and the face curved round the back and the top of the bar (the joystick's hole, a cup round each button's hole, the ridge), hollow inside and open toward the bar for the keypad and the switch carriers; 2 hinge knuckles at the back, the front screw's insert
collar_top.material: ASA (PETG for a first try), 100% infill round the ring. On its flat switch-cube side

collar_bottom.name: Collar bottom (with the bay)
collar_bottom.what: The smooth body's lower half: the ring's bottom and the electronics bay (the ESP32-C3 and the CAN transceiver on edge inside); the middle hinge knuckle, 2 M2 inserts for its cap; the front screw comes up through it into the top half
collar_bottom.material: ASA / PETG, 100% infill round the ring. On its flat switch-cube side

carrier_joy.name: Switch carrier: joystick + button 1
carrier_joy.what: Holds the 5-way switch and button 1's tactile switch in flat pockets (their legs through it, soldered to the wires in the channel underneath); goes up into the top half from the bar's side, first, pressing the keypad's skirt against the face
carrier_joy.material: ASA / PETG. On its flat switch-cube side

carrier_btn.name: Switch carrier: buttons 2-4
carrier_btn.what: Holds the other tactile switches (buttons 2 to 4; button 2 only with 2 buttons) the same way; goes in after the joystick's carrier
carrier_btn.material: ASA / PETG. On its flat switch-cube side

keypad.name: Keypad
keypad.what: A TPU liner inside the face, in one piece: the sheet under the face (its hollow domes are the buttons, round and pills; it hugs the joystick cap's sleeve) and a skirt round its edge that the carriers squeeze against the face: the seal
keypad.material: TPU 85A-95A. As an arch, its sheet on top (supports under it)

joy_cap.name: Joystick cap
joy_cap.what: A low 13 mm mushroom cap that pushes onto the 5-way switch's stem
joy_cap.material: ASA / PETG, or TPU for grip. Flat top down

bay_cap.name: Bay cap
bay_cap.what: A rounded dish that closes the bay from below (2 M2 x 6 countersunk); the dash's 4-core cable comes in through it

bay_gasket.name: Bay gasket
bay_gasket.what: Between the bay and its cap, squeezed 0.2 mm

remote_assembled.name: Assembled
remote_assembled.what: The collar on the bar, with stand-ins for the grip, the switch cube and the boards

params.name: buttons
params.label: Buttons
choices: 4 (up over the top of the bar)
params.help: In one column above the joystick: the collar is too narrow for two.

params.name: bar_d
params.label: Handlebar diameter
params.help: 22.2 (7/8") or 25.4 (1"). A bigger bar puts the face higher: the model refuses anything above the switch cube's top.

params.name: gap_w
params.label: Gap between the grip and the switch cube
params.help: The collar is 1 mm narrower. Slide the switch cube inboard to make room.

params.name: joy_a
params.label: Where the joystick sits, round the bar
params.help: From straight forward: 180 = straight back toward you, level with the bar's centre; 195 = a little below it. The buttons follow it up over the top.

params.name: pod_tilt
params.label: Controls tilted toward the grip
params.help: So your thumb reaches them straight from the grip.

params.name: nav_top
params.label: Joystick: the stem's top above its base
params.help: Too short and its cap can't grip it (the model says so).
